findings.description: The wrapper now shares and clears a single statistics dict on every call. Every call of the wrapped function, including concurrent or nested ones, reuses and clears the same dict object. The previous code gave each call its own copy's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs concurrently in threads or asyncio tasks, or recursively. Mechanism: stats.clear() wipes the dict that an in-flight call is still updating, and both calls write into the same dict through copy._local.statistics. Impact: attempt_number, delay_since_first_attempt and idle_for become corrupted or mixed between calls, and the mixing can also make retry decisions wrong.

findings.description: The async wrapper clears and shares one statistics dict across all calls, so concurrent tasks calling the same decorated coroutine function overwrite each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same retry-decorated coroutine function. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() and then reuses the same dict object, so the calls reset and mix each other's counters. Impact: statistics are wrong and attempt_number is corrupted. Anything that reads attempt_number, such as a stop_after_attempt condition, can misbehave.
